chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya Al-Azraq, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a person performing Tamattu' who had with him the price of a sacrificial animal (Hadayy), and he could have found a sacrificial animal equivalent to what he had with him. But he did not cease to hesitate and delay that until, when it was the end of the day, the price of sheep increased, so he was not able to buy a sacrificial animal with what he had. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast three days after the Days of Tashreeq.'

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrer performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.هَدْيٍ: Sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrer

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrificial animal due to delayed purchase?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the issue of *fidya* for a pilgrim performing *Tamattu'* who delays buying the sacrificial animal until the price becomes prohibitive is addressed. The Imam prescribes fasting for three days after the Days of Tashreeq as compensation, highlighting the flexibility in expiation when financial hardship arises due to delay rather than negligence. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the penalty is tied to the inability to fulfill the obligation at the prescribed time.
